Architectural Guide & Standards

What is Model Context Protocol (MCP)? The Universal AI Tooling Standard

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol open-sourced by Anthropic that standardizes how Artificial Intelligence applications securely connect to external tools, databases, APIs, and file systems. Prior to MCP, every AI agent framework required custom, ad-hoc integrations. MCP establishes a universal, client-agnostic standard using JSON-RPC 2.0 messages over standard input/output (stdio) or Server-Sent Events (SSE).

🛠️

1. Executable Tools

Model-callable functions with strict JSON schema definitions for running SQL queries, creating GitHub PRs, automating browsers, or sending Slack notifications.

📄

2. Contextual Resources

File-like read interfaces providing real-time data, database schema inspections, live logs, or external documentation directly into the model's active context window.

💡

3. Pre-Engineered Prompts

Standardized prompt templates and system directives created by tool authors to guide the LLM's multi-step decision-making and tool chaining reliably.

🛡️ How MCPShelf's 0-10 Trust Score Security Rating Works

Every server indexed on MCPShelf undergoes automated validation against official MCP specifications. Our pipeline audits npm/PyPI package integrity, checks static AST dependencies, inspects permission declarations (such as filesystem write vs read-only, socket networking, or arbitrary process execution), and incorporates community reviews to assign a cryptographic 0.0 to 10.0 Trust Score.

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything You Need to Know About MCPShelf

Quick answers for AI engineers, developers, and autonomous agent builders.

What is MCPShelf and how does it differ from other registries? ▾
MCPShelf is the open, community-curated Model Context Protocol registry and AI Agent Stack Builder. Unlike basic directories, MCPShelf provides full-text multi-token OmniSearch (<0.5ms debounce), independent 0-10 Trust Score security audits, capability matrix tagging, an interactive terminal TUI (npx @ritualdev-lab/mcpshelf explore), and a multi-server bundle cart that exports merged configuration files for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, and Zed in one click.
How do I install an MCP server into Claude Desktop? ▾
Open Claude Desktop, navigate to Settings > Developer > Edit Config to open your claude_desktop_config.json file. On MCPShelf, click "Install" on any server card, copy the generated JSON block into your mcpServers object, save the file, and restart Claude Desktop. The new tools will appear instantly with a hammer icon in your chat window.
What is the MCPShelf AI Agent Stack Builder? ▾
The AI Agent Stack Builder is a shopping-cart-like workflow tool. Click "+ Stack" on multiple servers (for example, PostgreSQL + GitHub + Slack + Puppeteer). MCPShelf dynamically merges them into a single configuration block for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Zed, and provides a shareable URL (?stack=...) so your entire engineering team can run the exact same agent tooling stack.
How are MCP servers audited and security scored? ▾
Every server is evaluated on a 0.0 to 10.0 Trust Score scale using automated JSON schema validation, static code analysis, permission scope auditing (such as filesystem read/write, network sockets, or subprocess spawning), community reviews, and transport sandboxing. Servers rated 9.5+ earn the Gold Security Shield badge.
Can I browse and configure MCP servers from the terminal? ▾
Yes! Run npx @ritualdev-lab/mcpshelf explore in any terminal. This launches an interactive, keyboard-driven Terminal User Interface (TUI) allowing you to search, filter by category, and copy client-ready JSON snippets without ever opening a web browser.
How can developers submit their own MCP server to MCPShelf? ▾
Developers can submit open-source MCP servers via our web portal at mcp.ritualdev.in/submit.html or programmatically via the automated REST API endpoint POST /api/v1/submit. Submissions undergo automated schema validation and initial security scoring upon receipt.
